title: refactor(plugin-security): move the everyone anchor, the explanation, the sharing verdicts and the authored-row write verdict out of security-plugin.ts (#25223 cut 10)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuMYdF2uchcinMphEKW4sYxd)_

Part of #25223
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Ruling-ref: 6353073966

Cut 10 of the `security-plugin.ts` split covers row 8 of the series plan: the everyone anchor, the explanation, the sharing verdicts and the authored-row write verdict. The claim is 6369634056. The row has four seams, so this one PR moves the bodies of ten methods out of the class, unedited, into four new modules. Cut 9 split its row the same way, over three.

To `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-everyone-anchor.ts`:

- `declareEveryone`: the `everyone` anchor's definition, as a started kernel derives it. It is the deployment's baseline plus every package default a `manage_metadata` holder accepted. Each withheld acceptance is reported with its reason (ADR-0090 D5/D7, ADR-0131 D3, #22801).
- `declareBuiltinPositions`: the six built-in positions, declared to the engine registry from `init()`. `everyone` names the fail-closed baseline (ADR-0131 D2). It is synchronous and stays synchronous.

To `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-explain-access.ts`:

- `explainAccessForCaller` (public): the `security/explain` answer for a caller. It covers:
  - who may explain whom (ADR-0090 D6, D12);
  - the explained user's context, built and vetted against the caller's organization;
  - the evaluation through the explain engine, with the CALLER as the asker of the record's read (#22792, #22851).

To `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts`:

- `resolveSharingReadFilter`: the owner/share half of the read scope. It throws on a resolution failure, so its callers fail closed (#4467).
- `resolveSharingCanEdit`: the sharing gate of a single-record write. It fails closed when the probe throws (#5386).
- `resolveWriteScopeForSharing`: the write-depth stash that both write probes hand the service (ADR-0057 D1).
- `resolveSharingWriteVerdict`: the tri-state write verdict (#5492, #6428).
- `resolvePreImageFloorDrop`: the floor decision of the by-id pre-image gate. `security/explain` asks it too (#19963).
- `delegatorOwnWriteFloorOptions`: the composition knobs the delegator's own direct by-id write would get (ADR-0090 D10).

To `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authored-row-write.ts`:

- `checkAuthoredRowWrite` (public): the `ISecurityService.checkAuthoredRowWrite` verdict, `admit` or `abstain` (#5493, #7281, #8059). The scope its probe read runs under moves with it: `AUTHORED_ROW_WRITE_PROBE_CONTEXT`, which nothing else reads.

The change is move-only, and the card stays open for `start()`. The branch is `claude/project-thread-3fzya4`, the harness-pinned branch for this session. It was restarted from `origin/main` at `05cc3ee953`, which contains cut 9's merge `dd124e9466`. The branch name names no issue, so the claim comment is the identity record.

**What stays in the class.** Each moved method keeps its name, signature, docblock and position, less `async`. Every caller still reaches the methods through the plugin:

- the `security` service binding (`explain`, `checkAuthoredRowWrite`);
- `init()` and `kernel:ready`;
- the middleware;
- the read scope;
- the master gate.

Two members of the row stay whole, `everyoneBaseline` (6 body lines) and `destroy` (3). Neither body is longer than its stub would be: `everyoneBaseline`'s stub would also be 6 lines.

**Module-level declarations.**

- `AUTHORED_ROW_WRITE_PROBE_CONTEXT` is read only by `checkAuthoredRowWrite`'s body. It moves with its docblock, unedited and still unexported, as cuts 1 to 4 and 9 moved declarations that only their bodies read. Its docblock's `{@link SecurityPlugin.checkAuthoredRowWrite}` resolves through the module's type import of the class.
- `absentUnderCallerRead` and `unreadableUnderCallerRead` stay in `security-plugin.ts`, and each gains `export` and nothing else. The explanation reads both. `absentUnderCallerRead` is shared with the write path's step 2.7, which stays. `unreadableUnderCallerRead` is defined and documented beside it. Its docblock links to `absentUnderCallerRead`, and cut 8's `security-plugin-addressed-writes.ts` header names both as living in `security-plugin.ts`.
- `requiredCapsForOperation` is already exported. The explanation imports it by value, as the object-admission module does.
- Import names that only the moved bodies read leave `security-plugin.ts`. The modules import them from the same specifiers:
  - `explainAccessForAsker` and `buildContextForUser` (`./explain-engine.js`);
  - the whole `./builtin-positions.js` import (`declareEveryoneBaseline`, `registerBuiltinPositions`);
  - `readAcceptedEveryoneSets` (`./suggested-audience-bindings.js`);
  - `readDeclaredCapabilityContext` (`./declared-capability-context.js`);
  - `vetOrganizationClaim` (`@objectstack/core`);
  - the type `ExplainOperation` (`@objectstack/spec/security`).

  No staying docblock links to any of them. Two staying docblocks name `readAcceptedEveryoneSets` and `vetOrganizationClaim`, in backticks only.
- The unexported interface `RlsFilterOptions` stays where every gate reads it. The explanation and the sharing verdicts name it through the class's own signature, as the type of `computeLayeredRlsFilter`'s fifth parameter less `undefined`, so the moved text names it exactly as before. Cut 9's modules name `ObjectSecurityMeta` the same way.
- Each value import is read only inside a function body, at call time, and never while a module evaluates. `index.ts` still exports only what it did, so the published surface does not move (measured below).

**Two readers outside the moved code read the moved lines by path. Both are re-pointed in this PR, as cut 9 re-pointed the same two.**

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`, row 9. `check-system-context-census` keys each elevation read by file and enclosing symbol, and `explainAccessForCaller`'s `callerContext?.isSystem` read now sits in the explain module.
  - A trial cut measured the page left untouched. The census reports 2 problems: the new file has no row, and the old anchor is no longer a read site.
  - The anchor keeps its symbol and changes only its path, from `security-plugin.ts#explainAccessForCaller` to `security-plugin-explain-access.ts#explainAccessForCaller`. No row's text changes.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-organization-membership.test.ts`, the #25107 enumeration pin. The explanation resolves a delegator and asks the organization check beside it. So the expected list gains `security-plugin-explain-access.ts`, and the title says seven files instead of six.
  - The rule it pins is unchanged: asks equal resolutions in every file. It holds at head: the explain module counts 1 and 1, and `security-plugin.ts` counts 1 and 1 (`start()`; it counted 2 and 2 at base).

**No ADR anchor entry is added.** No paragraph of the `security-plugin.ts` entry describes these bodies (see ADR anchors below).

**One receiver changes, disclosed.** `resolveKernelService` is a function-valued field. The explanation and three of the sharing verdicts call it through the host, so its `this` is now the host, not the plugin. Two facts keep every call answering as it did:

- the only function ever assigned to the field is the arrow function `start()` assigns, which returns `ctx.getService(name)` and answers `undefined` when that throws, and it reads no `this`;
- no test or other file assigns the field.

Cut 9's report said that no body it moved calls a function-valued field. This cut's bodies do, so it is stated here.

## The published `.d.ts` does not change

Measured under the series bar (ruling 6348891160 item 1), on base `05cc3ee953` and on head `38392cb1b7`. Each was a full `turbo run build` in its own worktree. A package build of the same trees before the claim gave the same bytes.

- Raw sha256 of `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.d.mts` is the same for all four files, base and head: `7d67966ce82e00a1531807b3b0008f16c489fc2c3199f9ad67078302eb2803da`. The raw diff is 0 lines, so no union order moved either. These are the same bytes cut 9 measured, so neither cut 9's merge nor main's later commits moved this package's `.d.ts`.
- Normalised sha256 is the same for all four: `b53e9025f794e20debd2245afed5ceb1a0ad48109a2a21cc19232a562ccd9cb4`.
- `security-plugin.ts` gains two exports, `absentUnderCallerRead` and `unreadableUnderCallerRead`. Each takes one read callback and answers a boolean promise, so its signature names no type from another module, so the cut 6 trap does not arise. `index.ts` re-exports neither.
- The normaliser, run from `packages/plugins/plugin-security`, sorts the members of each string-literal union and changes nothing else:

```sh
node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8");process.stdout.write(s.replace(/"[^"\n]*"(?:\s*\|\s*"[^"\n]*")+/g,r=>r.split(/\s*\|\s*/).sort().join(" | ")))' dist/index.d.ts | sha256sum
```

- Positive controls, each a one-line edit on a copy of the head `dist/index.d.ts`:
  - line 557 (`private resolveSharingReadFilter;`) made public: raw `8c8fad488058d08a54e23b5410b539b7eecad71a0e749b0133a61280e146bdde`, normalised `f02f50957a57e31fd943e00fa0ef74113a2f0efdc4af8e3ee5b963c7e932a3c6`;
  - line 447 renamed (`private declareEveryoneRenamed;`): raw `7af56294d477cdbc07b22567c87a110bbc2c36d37724cc47ed3652dc085a8ab4`, normalised `44d50a2b10e166373f11f31ef5e046c1a05ab9f5613e9d6b762c03c7ca15ec88`;
  - line 745, the public `checkAuthoredRowWrite` signature, with `context?: any` changed to `context?: unknown`: raw `b75e990785a61245092adf8414acba79b6fe27f330ebd7555e9a808642802556`, normalised `6b7331a568193fda94c1e45eabe85f5704d61c6ef99639bb197b7f11510b81b6`.

  All three differ from the real hashes, so the comparison does see a visibility change, a rename and a change to a public signature.
- The two public methods carry their full signatures and docblocks in the `.d.ts`: `explainAccessForCaller` (line 525) and `checkAuthoredRowWrite` (745). The eight private methods carry only their name and docblock: `declareEveryone` (447), `declareBuiltinPositions` (483), and the six sharing verdicts (557 to 676). Those lines are the same in both files.
- Export tables: the ESM and CJS bundles each export the same 66 names at base and at head. The lists were loaded at runtime, with `require` and `import()` of the built bundles, not parsed. The sorted name list hashes to `83576430f83cf60cecbcc5c0e80214f16c626a8e66f700294fc6a44361423116` for all four, as at cuts 6 to 9.
- The bundle JS bytes differ, because code moved within them: `index.js` goes from `dfa83a54` to `78d8f0eb`, and `index.mjs` from `18c4d919` to `5d290484`. Every value the new modules import comes from a file inside this package or from a specifier `security-plugin.ts` already imports. So the set of external specifiers each bundle loads is the same at base and head: 16 distinct `require` specifiers in `index.js` and 19 distinct `from` specifiers in `index.mjs`.
- Bundle order, disclosed: `builtin-positions.ts`, `manifest.ts` and `objects/sys-audience-binding-suggestion.object.ts` are now emitted just ahead of the four modules, where before they sat between `security-plugin.ts`'s chunks. None of them imports `security-plugin.ts`, and their top level only declares constants.

No changeset: `skip-changeset`, per ruling 6348891160 item 4.

## What moved

The base line numbers are each method's signature and closing brace at `05cc3ee953`. The last column lists the members the body reads, which is exactly what its host carries.

| method | base lines | module | host members |
|---|---|---|---|

| `explainAccessForCaller` (public, async) | `:5061`-`:5373` | explain-access | `baselinePermissionSets`, `checkControlledByParentWrite`, `computeLayeredRlsFilter`, `computeReadPartialMaskRules`, `computeRlsFilter`, `delegatedAdminGate`, `foldFieldRequiredPermissions`, `getObjectSecurityMeta`, `permissionEvaluator`, `ql`, `readRowById`, `resolveKernelService`, `resolvePermissionSetsForContext`, `resolvePreImageFloorDrop`, `resolveSharingReadFilter`, `resolveWriteScopeForSharing`, `tenancyPosture` |

| `resolveSharingWriteVerdict` (private, async) | `:5563`-`:5593` | sharing-verdicts | `logger`, `resolveKernelService`, `resolveWriteScopeForSharing` |
| `resolvePreImageFloorDrop` (private, async) | `:5621`-`:5642` | sharing-verdicts | `collectRLSPolicies`, `resolveSharingWriteVerdict` |

Each async stub drops `async` and returns the moved function's promise, as cuts 1 and 3 to 9 did for their async methods. `declareBuiltinPositions` was synchronous, and its stub returns its function's `void`. Two of the ten are public, so the `.d.ts` carries their full signatures. A body move does not touch a signature, and those lines do not change (above).

## The shape (#23050 shape B, as cuts 1 to 9 applied it)

- The class keeps each method with its name, signature, docblock and position, because tsup emits members with their JSDoc into the `.d.ts`. Each body is now one host literal plus `fn.call(host, …)`, marked `[#25223 cut 10]`.
- `EveryoneAnchorHost`, `ExplainAccessHost`, `SharingVerdictsHost` and `AuthoredRowWriteHost` are new. Each types every member as the class member itself (`SecurityPlugin['m']`). Each moved function types its `this` as the `Pick` of its host over exactly the members its body reads, and the stub annotates its literal with the same `Pick`. There is no cast, and no member becomes public or protected.
- Methods go in as late-bound closures that call `this.m(...a)` on the plugin at call time. So a spy or test double set on the plugin is still the one the body reaches:
  - the everyone declarations still ask the plugin's baseline and deployment acceptance;
  - the explanation still asks the plugin's set resolution, RLS filters, sharing read filter, write-depth stash, floor decision, controlled-by-parent check, field folds, posture reader and by-id read;
  - the sharing verdicts still ask the plugin's set resolution, posture reader and RLS policy collection, and they still ask each other through the plugin;
  - the authored-row verdict still asks the plugin's set resolution, policy collection and layered RLS filter.

  No test replaces a moved method on the plugin instance today. One that did would still replace it for every caller.
- Fields follow the rule cut 1 set, judged on each field's own declaration:
  - `baselinePermissionSets` is declared `readonly`, so it goes by value.
  - None of the other eight fields the bodies read is declared `readonly`: `delegatedAdminGate`, `epoch`, `logger`, `metadata`, `permissionEvaluator`, `ql`, `resolveKernelService` and `tenancyPosture`. So they go as getters, and each read happens when the body makes it. `start()` assigns all of them except `permissionEvaluator` after construction, and tests replace `permissionEvaluator` on a constructed plugin.
  - `delegatedAdminGate`, `epoch`, `logger`, `permissionEvaluator` and `ql` are objects whose own methods the bodies call. `resolveKernelService` is the one function-valued field (disclosed above).
  - The hosts declare every field `readonly`, so a moved body cannot assign a member through them. The typecheck passes, so none does.
- Nothing re-exports any of the modules, so the package entry does not move.

## Proof of move-only

- **Bodies, by AST token.** Each moved function's body has the same TypeScript token sequence as the base method body. Each of the 549 body lines is the base line with two leading spaces removed. Parameters, return types and `async` match.
  - The explanation's body holds five multi-line JSDoc text tokens, the docblocks of its inner closures. Their continuation lines are re-indented one level, like every other body line. So the comparison dedents those JSDoc tokens one level, and only those. A string or template token that spans lines is compared byte for byte. The explanation's 1,731 tokens are then equal.
  - Four negative controls fail the check:
    - in `explainAccessForCaller`, `callerContext?.isSystem === true` changed to `=== false`;
    - in `resolveSharingCanEdit`, the fail-closed `return false;` of the probe's `catch` changed to `return true;`;
    - in `checkAuthoredRowWrite`, the non-write abstention `return 'abstain';` changed to `return 'admit';`;
    - in one of the explanation's inner JSDoc blocks, "The two contexts" changed to "The three contexts". This control shows that the JSDoc dedent does not hide a change of words.
- **Class side.** Each moved method keeps its docblock and signature, less `async`. Every other class member is byte-identical to base: 116 named members plus the constructor, including `everyoneBaseline` and `destroy`. The class has 127 members at base and at head.
- **Top level of `security-plugin.ts`.** Of the 106 top-level statements at base other than the class, 97 are byte-identical at head. The other nine:
  - five imports each lose the names listed above, and the `./builtin-positions.js` import is gone;
  - `AUTHORED_ROW_WRITE_PROBE_CONTEXT` is gone from the file. The authored-row module holds the same statement and docblock, byte for byte;
  - `absentUnderCallerRead` and `unreadableUnderCallerRead` are the base text with `export` added.

  The four new statements are the imports of the new modules.
- **The two re-pointed readers.** The page diff is one line, the anchor's path. The pin diff is the title's count and one added list entry.
- **git's own view.** This is `git diff --color-moved=plain --color-moved-ws=allow-indentation-change 05cc3ee953 HEAD` over the five source files. Of the 596 deleted lines, git sees 581 as moved. The other 15 are the nine signatures that lose `async`, four of the import lines that change, and the two functions that gain `export`. Of the 1,184 added lines, 679 show as moved: 669 in the four modules, and 10 in `security-plugin.ts` whose text git also finds among the deleted lines (nine stub `};` lines and the host line `baselinePermissionSets: this.baselinePermissionSets,`). The rest are the modules' headers, imports, host interfaces, type aliases and function signatures, the ten stubs, and the four new imports with their comments.
- **Size.** 1,785 changed lines (+1,187 / -598) over 7 files, under the 3,000-line manual-merge line.
  - `security-plugin.ts` goes from 8,852 to 8,406 lines.
  - `security-plugin-everyone-anchor.ts` has 140 lines, `security-plugin-explain-access.ts` 433, `security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts` 277 and `security-plugin-authored-row-write.ts` 184.
  - The other two files are the page (+1 / -1) and the pin (+2 / -1).

## ADR anchors (ruling 6353073966 item 2)

- `node scripts/check-adr-symbol-anchors.mjs` exits 0 and gives byte-identical output at base `05cc3ee953` and at head. `dispatch-gates --commands` does not derive it for this change set, so it was run by hand.
- `pnpm check:adr-anchors` exits 0 at base and at head, with 81 anchored files at both ends.
- **No new entry.** No paragraph of the `security-plugin.ts` entry describes a moved body:
  - ADR-0055 §1 is the controlled-by-parent relation (cuts 2 to 4);
  - ADR-0106 D7 is the projection asymmetry (cut 9's field-readers module carries it);
  - ADR-0123 D2 is the write wall's no-organization refusal (cut 5);
  - ADR-0138 D1 is the seed-ownership claim.

  So no module of this cut gets an entry, as the modules of cuts 1 and 6 to 8 have none.
- **The decision-letter count on the anchored surface goes from 1978 to 1969.** That gate counts `ADR-NNNN Dk` citations in each anchored file and in each entry's own invariant text. Nine citations leave the anchored surface with the moved bodies:
  - `explainAccessForCaller` 7: ADR-0090 D6, ADR-0090 D10, ADR-0090 D12, ADR-0105 D3 twice, ADR-0111 D3, ADR-0111 D5;
  - `resolveSharingReadFilter` 1: ADR-0057 D1;
  - `checkAuthoredRowWrite` 1: ADR-0058 D4.

  The other bodies, the moved constant's docblock, the four module headers and the four new import comments cite none.

  `resolveSharingReadFilter`'s `depth` parameter comment also cites ADR-0090 D10. The parameter list belongs to the signature, which stays in the class, so that letter stays on the anchored surface. The move copies each signature unedited, so the function's parameter list carries it too.

  Measured directly: `security-plugin.ts` holds 258 such citations at base and 249 at head, and the 9 that leave are exactly these.
- Every moved citation is still in the tree, in the module its body moved to. Citations that resolve tree-wide go from 52223 across 6651 files at base to 52224 across 6654 at head. Three of the modules cite an ADR. The one added citation is the `depth` parameter comment, which both signatures now carry.
- `docs/adr/**` is not touched, and no anchor token is planted.
- The anchor map covers every ADR symbol anchor that names `security-plugin.ts`: 27 anchors over 18 symbols.
  - It was measured with `extractAnchors` and `symbolSegmentResolution` from `scripts/symbol-anchors.mjs`. That is measurement, not a new gate.
  - It was read on `05cc3ee953` BEFORE the claim, with the whole cut applied as a local trial, and no anchor changed class.
  - No ADR anchors a row 8 member or the moved constant. Every anchor resolves at head in `security-plugin.ts`, with its base class.

## Readers

Two readers outside the moved code read the moved lines by path: the system-context page and the #25107 enumeration pin. Both are re-pointed in this PR (above). No other gate, baseline, docs anchor or test reads the moved lines by path. Each kind was read:

- **The system-context census.**
  - `node scripts/isystem-census.mjs --json` gives the same 148 sites at base and at head, 0 differences. The comparison ignores line numbers and maps the four modules back to `security-plugin.ts`.
  - One head site is in the modules: `explainAccessForCaller`'s `callerContext?.isSystem` read, which the page's re-pointed anchor names. The moved bodies' `isSystem: true` keys and the probe constant's key are counted the same way at both ends.
  - The role counts are the same (`read` 153, `declaration` 38, `key` 438, `other` 9), and so are the 5 non-elevation reads and the 22 packages. The files holding a site go from 74 to 75, and the scanned files from 397 to 399, the two modules that name `isSystem`.
  - `check-system-context-census` and its `--self-test` exit 0 at base and at head. The totals are the same (148 sites, 127 symbols, 140 cited against 140 required, 163 anchors), and files go from 74 to 75. With the page left untouched, it reports 2 problems (claim).
- **The tenant-audit census.** No moved body holds an engine write. The explanation and the authored-row verdict read through `ql.findOne` and `ql.find`, and the everyone declaration hands `ql` to the derivation's readers. `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --json` gives the same 238 write call sites at base and at head, compared the same way: 0 differences, none in the modules, and the same 175 non-engine calls. Only `scannedSources` moves, from 730 to 734, the four modules. `check-tenant-audit-census` exits 0 at base and at head with the same output, and `tenant-audit-census.mdx` is not touched.
